bu.tieu_de: Shore up control: numbers and standards
bu.viec: Pick 3 numbers the whole team reviews weekly (revenue, cost, defects) and one person who owns the sheet. Any spend above an agreed amount needs two approvers.
bu.cach_do: After 4 weeks: was the sheet updated all 4 times?

troi.tieu_de: Control-heavy team: keep process from blocking new work
troi.viec: Each month, reserve one small task for trying a new approach, with a small budget agreed in advance.

bu.tieu_de: Shore up growth: new work and long-range plans
bu.viec: Give one person the list of new opportunities (clients, channels, products); each month pick one to test small.
bu.cach_do: After 4 weeks: at least one small test has finished with a result.

troi.tieu_de: Growth-heavy team: finish before you start
troi.viec: Agree that a new project only opens when the running one has an owner for the final finishing work.

bu.tieu_de: Shore up outreach: listen to clients and the market
bu.viec: Each week one person calls 3 existing clients to ask what else they need, then writes one short page for the team.
bu.cach_do: After 4 weeks: 12 calls and at least one small change based on client feedback.

troi.tieu_de: Analysis-heavy team: put a deadline on discussion
troi.viec: Every decision gets a decision date. If information is still missing by then, pick the safest option and move.

bu.tieu_de: Shore up the front line: sales and communication
bu.viec: Hold a 20-minute weekly round where someone retells a recent win and why the client bought; name one person to speak for the team with new clients.
bu.cach_do: After 4 weeks: does the team have a one-minute pitch everyone can say?

troi.tieu_de: Front-line-heavy team: keep clients after the sale
troi.viec: Attach every closed deal to one follow-up step with a date and an owner.

bu.tieu_de: Shore up operations: process and handover
bu.viec: Write a 5-step checklist for the team's most repeated task, post it where everyone sees it, and have one person review it at day's end.
bu.cach_do: After 4 weeks: fewer redo's caused by a missed step.

troi.tieu_de: Operations-heavy team: leave room for change
troi.viec: Each quarter, review one old process and drop steps no longer needed; ask the people who do the work before changing it.

quy_che.tieu_de: Agree on how you discuss work with {ten}
quy_che.viec: You two tend to clash head-on. Settle who decides what, put big items in writing as 3 bullet points, and avoid debating in front of the team.
quy_che.vi_sao: Your zodiac signs clash, or you are both used to being the one who decides.

bu_khuyet.tieu_de: Hand the work you tend to miss to {ten}
bu_khuyet.viec: You are light on {hanh}; this person is strong exactly there. Give them a whole stream of that work and agree on a results check every two weeks.
bu_khuyet.vi_sao: Their leading element fills the element you lack.

ghep_cap.viec: These two are strong on different axes. Give them one 4-week project, each owning a clear half.
ghep_cap.vi_sao: The two axes complement each other: one opens work, one keeps it going.

mot_mot.viec: In the last week, book 15 minutes with each person. Use the two suggested questions on their card, listen and take notes, and promise nothing yet.
mot_mot.vi_sao: Collaboration tips only help when they match what the person actually tells you.

bu_truc.vi_sao: The team's lightest element is {hanh}, the axis of {vai_tro}.

troi_truc.vi_sao: The whole team leans toward {hanh}, strong in {vai_tro}, so the opposite side is easy to miss.

phan_bien_cang.van_de: A strong specialist who pushes back hard and is hard to give feedback to
phan_bien_cang.goc_nhin: {ten} is used to deciding alone and needs to see clear standards before taking on work. Given orders without reasons, this kind of person tends to argue back.
phan_bien_cang.mo_loi: "I need your critical view on this. Let's agree the output standard first; how you get there is your call."
phan_bien_cang.viec: Set the goal and the standard, let them choose the method, and give feedback in private, not in front of the team.

ban_hang_sot_quy_trinh.van_de: A fast, keen team that keeps skipping process and reports
ban_hang_sot_quy_trinh.goc_nhin: The whole team leans toward {hanh_troi} (moves fast, likes meeting people) and is light on {hanh_thieu} (keeping process, checking detail).
ban_hang_sot_quy_trinh.mo_loi: "We keep the same selling pace and just add 3 end-of-day steps so no client slips through."
ban_hang_sot_quy_trinh.viec: Turn repeated data entry into a 3-step end-of-day checklist and have one person cross-check.

hai_truc_va_cham.van_de: Two key people are both good, but meetings with both get tense
hai_truc_va_cham.goc_nhin: {ten_a} leans toward growth and wants speed; {ten_b} leans toward control and wants certainty at each step. Both are right from their side.
hai_truc_va_cham.mo_loi: "The first 15 minutes are for {ten_a} to propose; the next 15 are for {ten_b} to check risks. No cutting in across the two parts."
hai_truc_va_cham.viec: Split the meeting into two timed parts; the final call belongs to one person named in advance.

nguoi_om_viec.van_de: Your most dedicated person keeps taking on too much
nguoi_om_viec.goc_nhin: {ten} tends to carry other people's work and finds it hard to say no.
nguoi_om_viec.mo_loi: "This week, list the tasks you're doing for other people. Let's hand them back to the right owners."
nguoi_om_viec.viec: Review their task list monthly and send back what isn't theirs.

y_tuong_nhieu.van_de: Plenty of ideas, but every project stays half-done
y_tuong_nhieu.goc_nhin: {ten} is strong at thinking up and starting work, while the whole team is light on {hanh_thieu}, the axis that carries work to the end.
y_tuong_nhieu.mo_loi: "Each time you start something new, pick one person to own the finishing with you."
y_tuong_nhieu.viec: Each person holds at most two open tasks; a third waits until one is done.

it_noi_trong_hop.van_de: Someone says little in meetings, then disagrees afterwards
it_noi_trong_hop.goc_nhin: {ten} thinks things through before speaking and avoids debating in a crowd.
it_noi_trong_hop.mo_loi: "Send me your view in writing before the meeting; I'll read your part out."
it_noi_trong_hop.viec: Send the agenda a day ahead, take written input, and check in with them privately after.

doi_nhip.van_de: A key person suddenly slows down
doi_nhip.goc_nhin: This year {ten} is in a {pha} phase in numerology, a stretch when people often want to change how they work or learn something new. Slowing down is not the same as getting worse.
doi_nhip.mo_loi: "What would you like to learn or try next quarter? Let's see if the team can give you that."
doi_nhip.viec: Ask before drawing conclusions; give them a new piece of work or have them train someone on the team.

giu_nhip.van_de: The team is doing fine. How do you keep it that way?
giu_nhip.goc_nhin: No clear friction point shows up in this team. What slips first is repeated work nobody reviews.
giu_nhip.mo_loi: "This month, everyone pick one task where we do an extra step, and we'll cut it together."
giu_nhip.viec: Hold a 30-minute monthly review of repeated work and keep what is working.

hoi: Which work would you like to own from start to finish?
When do you feel watched too closely?
1.manh: You do well owning work end to end and choosing your own method.
1.de_y: Under pressure you tend to do everything yourself instead of sharing. Tell your manager early which parts you are holding.
1.lam_tot: Clear goals, clear decision rights, little interference midway.
1.trao_doi: Say plainly what you need to decide, with a date for reporting results.

hoi: Is there something that isn't working that you haven't felt able to say?
On what kind of work would you like to be asked for your view?
2.manh: You keep things calm between people and notice others' feelings early.
2.de_y: You tend to keep disagreement to yourself. Write one sentence before the meeting and send it.
2.lam_tot: A team with little friction and someone who listens to private input.
2.trao_doi: Send your view in writing first, then speak briefly in the meeting.

hoi: Which idea would you most like to try this quarter?
Which work do you tend to leave unfinished, and who could help with the end?
3.manh: You are strong on ideas, persuasive in conversation, and lift the team's mood.
3.de_y: You tend to open many things at once. Keep at most two tasks in progress.
3.lam_tot: Room to try new ideas and someone who shares the finishing.
3.trao_doi: Bring an idea with one small test step and a finish date.

hoi: Which process feels like too much or too little?
When plans change, what do you need to know first?
4.manh: You work systematically and carefully, and are trusted wherever precision matters.
4.de_y: You slow down when plans change suddenly. Ask for the reason and the transition plan as soon as you hear.
4.lam_tot: Work with a process, clear deadlines and few changes midway.
4.trao_doi: Propose with a concrete list of steps and the risks you see.

hoi: Which task feels repetitive to the point of boredom?
Which new area would you like to try?
5.manh: You learn fast, handle surprises well and suit new areas.
5.de_y: Long repetitive work bores you quickly. Set yourself a new goal each quarter instead of waiting to be given one.
5.lam_tot: Goals that change by quarter and room to try new approaches.
5.trao_doi: Say clearly what you want to change and what you will keep.

hoi: Which work are you doing in place of someone else?
Which part would you like me to take off your hands?
6.manh: You are dedicated and responsible toward teammates and clients, and suit care and retention roles.
6.de_y: You tend to carry others' work. Each month, list what isn't yours and hand it back.
6.lam_tot: Clearly bounded work and someone to share the load when it is busy.
6.trao_doi: Say early when you are overloaded, with the work you suggest moving to someone else.

hoi: What gap do you see in how the team works?
Do you prefer to discuss in writing or in person?
7.manh: You analyse deeply and spot gaps early; you suit specialist and quality roles.
7.de_y: You speak little in large meetings. Send your comments in writing beforehand.
7.lam_tot: Time for focused work and few formal meetings.
7.trao_doi: Keep it short and based on concrete facts.

hoi: At what target level would you feel the workload is right?
Which authority still feels unclear?
8.manh: You have a sharp eye for numbers, targets and resources, and suit leading an area with targets.
8.de_y: When authority lines are unclear you tend to clash. Ask early what you can decide.
8.lam_tot: Measurable goals, clear authority and rewards tied to results.
8.trao_doi: Go straight to the numbers and your proposal.

hoi: Which work feels most meaningful to you?
For that big goal, which number shall we track?
9.manh: You see the big picture and care about people; you suit brand and long-range projects.
9.de_y: You tend to put ideals ahead of short-term numbers. Tie each big goal to one measurable indicator.
9.lam_tot: Work with a clear purpose and milestones to measure.
9.trao_doi: Say why the work matters, with the number you will track.

hoi: What trend are you seeing that the team hasn't noticed?
What on the team tires you most?
11.manh: You sense trends and people's feelings; you suit advisory and creative roles.
11.de_y: Long periods of disorder wear you out fast. Speak up early when the team feels chaotic.
11.lam_tot: A transparent team with little internal politics.
11.trao_doi: Share what you sense along with the concrete signs you noticed.

hoi: Which system would you like to build this year?
How many phases shall we split that big job into?
22.manh: You can build large systems and turn long-range plans into working practice.
22.de_y: You set very high expectations for yourself and others. Split goals into short phases.
22.lam_tot: Freedom to design how things work and time for long projects.
22.trao_doi: Present by phase, with one result per phase.

hoi: Who on the team are you mentoring?
Which standard is hard to hold when you care about someone?
33.manh: You are good at mentoring people, raising team skill and keeping clients' trust.
33.de_y: You tend to relax standards out of kindness. Hold to the standards the team agreed.
33.lam_tot: Mentoring newcomers, with shared standards for the whole team.
33.trao_doi: Say who you are mentoring and what you need to do it well.

ca_nhan.ve_nhom: The person who invited you will see your zodiac sign, strongest element, life path, personal year and collaboration tips, not your birth date.
ca_nhan.nhan_trao_doi: How to talk with your manager
